Tennis legend Rafael Nadal has been elected to the board of directors of Spanish football club Real Madrid after receiving 99.5 per cent of votes at the club’s Extraordinary General Assembly. The 22-time Grand Slam champion was ratified as a board member on Saturday during the assembly held at the basketball pavilion of the club’s Ciudad Real Madrid training complex. According to an announcement on Real Madrid’s website on Saturday, 1,704 of the 1,713 votes cast were in favour of Nadal’s appointment, with four against and five abstentions. Nadal, who has been an honorary member of the club since 2011, received a standing ovation from the club’s representative members following the vote. Reacting to his appointment, the 40-year-old Spaniard described the position as a major responsibility and expressed his desire to contribute to the club’s future. This club is passed down from parents to children and unites people. For me, it connects me with family and friends to watch matches together. It’s an immense joy and a great satisfaction. It is an infinite responsibility, and I take it on with the hope of learning and contributing so that this club continues to be the best in the world,” he said. Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez welcomed Nadal’s appointment, describing him as a sporting legend whose influence extended beyond his achievements on the tennis court. Pérez said Nadal’s inclusion in the board represented more than the arrival of a celebrated athlete, adding that the tennis star wanted to share the responsibility of shaping the club’s future. Nadal is one of the most successful tennis players in history, having won 22 Grand Slam singles titles, including a record 14 French Open championships. He also won two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cup titles with Spain and spent time as world number one during his career.
